rows.label: Discount rate
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact discounts at 0.04 a year. Linked to the shared discount rate (Your values); the evaluator view pins it to Ambitious Impact's rate.
rows.formula: $discount_rate

rows.label: Fixed charity costs
rows.explainer: Fixed costs of starting the charity. $100k set up costs assumed.

rows.label: Charity costs (Expected)
rows.formula: if(1, fixed_charity_costs, 0)

rows.label: Year number (year 2)
rows.explainer: Calculated in the source sheet as `=if(B38+1<=round($B$13+$B$28,0), B38+1, "-")`; kept as a fixed number here (text in arithmetic).

rows.label: Stopping point if charity is unsuccessful
rows.explainer: If after 5 years it looks unlikely the charity will be successful, we assume they will end the operation. Costs after this point will therefore be incurred probabilistically.

rows.label: Ongoing charity costs
rows.explainer:
Costs roughly based on 4 staff members plus additional buffer.

Range from Ambitious Impact's uncertainty tab (CEA!C:D, its 95% interval for a normal draw): 100000 to 400000.

rows.label: Charity years operating
rows.explainer: Implementation period - from WHO CEA guidelines: https://www.who.int/choice/publications/p_2003_generalised_cea.pdf

rows.label: Reduced ongoing charity costs
rows.formula: ongoing_charity_costs / 2

rows.label: Counterfactual impact
rows.explainer:
This is the proportion of the impact which can be assigned to the charity which would not happen otherwise. It is quite high, as even though a lot of work has been done on this issue, it is not currently a centre stage issue and is quite difficult for organizations to get funding for it. I think it is likely that this intervention won't be introduced in many countries, so we could probably find a country where it would have large counterfactual value. However the actual figure is an intuitive assumption.

Range from Ambitious Impact's uncertainty tab (CEA!C:D, its 95% interval for a normal draw): 0.65 to 0.95.

rows.label: Probability of success
rows.explainer:
The probability that the price increase will be implemented. Probability assumed low because it's difficult to get policy change passed, and there's likely to be industry resistance to this policy. See main report for further discussion.

Range from Ambitious Impact's uncertainty tab (CEA!C:D, its 95% interval for a normal draw): 0.015 to 0.095.

rows.label: Country growth rate
rows.explainer: Changed for consistency. Ambitious Impact's sheet grows each year's health benefit (DALYs × income × 2.8) and income benefit by income growth, 2.6% a year (World Bank, range 2.08–3.12%), then turns the total back into DALY equivalents at today's income. That counts a DALY averted in year t as 1.026^t DALYs, about 1.6 DALYs by year 18, when the benefits start. Growth is the only thing this row feeds, so our view sets it to 0, which counts every year's DALY as one DALY; the evaluator view keeps AIM's 2.6%.

summary: Ambitious Impact's 2020 estimate for a new charity advocating for a 50% rise in alcohol excise taxes in an average Sub-Saharan African country, counting health and income gains from lower drinking. The idea the Center for Alcohol Policy Solutions was founded to run. A re-implementation of the sheet's point-estimate tab ($98 per DALY equivalent); the report's headline, about $96 (a benefit-cost ratio of 115:1), is the mean of a Monte Carlo simulation. In our view a DALY averted in a later year isn't inflated by income growth.
